claims.text: Adding a low volume fraction of nanostructured AlN particles to an HEA intermediate layer will improve its heat-transfer capability.
Adding nanostructured AlN particles will preserve the HEA intermediate layer's structural integrity under high-temperature mechanical loading.
A low particle concentration can facilitate a stable and homogeneous dispersion at elevated temperature.
AlN nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed within a solid HEA intermediate layer during processing.
Dispersed AlN nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries in the HEA.
Grain-boundary pinning by AlN nanoparticles will mitigate grain coarsening.
AlN nanoparticles will reinforce the HEA microstructure.
AlN has sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to create additional heat-conduction pathways in the HEA.
Homogeneously dispersed AlN particles will produce Zener pinning in the HEA.
Zener pinning will stabilize HEA grain size under thermal and mechanical stresses.
The AlN-modified HEA will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable HEA intermediate layer without AlN.
The AlN-modified HEA will retain similar or greater tensile strength than the unmodified HEA.
The AlN-modified HEA will have similar or improved microstructural stability relative to the unmodified HEA.
The proposed benefits will persist during thermal cycling to approximately 800 degrees Celsius and under mechanical loads representative of plasma-facing components.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on AlN volume fraction and dispersion quality.
Long-term particle-dispersion stability under prolonged high-temperature conditions is uncertain.
